title: Steering: reduce patient call-center wait times

items.text: Staff to the arrival pattern: Monday 8-11 gets 22% of calls while everyone works an identical 8-5 shift; measure demand by interval and stagger/shift schedules
paraphrases: Monday 8-11 is 22% of weekly volume but staffing is flat - realign shifts to the peak.
Pull call volume by 30-minute interval and stagger agent schedules to match the arrival pattern.
Staff to demand by interval (Erlang-style), not to a flat 8-5 shift.
negatives: Hire more agents to reduce waits.

items.text: Remove refill-status calls (31%) at the source: proactive text/portal status updates and pharmacy notifications
paraphrases: 31% of calls ask about refill status - send proactive text updates so patients don't need to call.
Deflect prescription-status calls with automated pharmacy notifications or self-service.
Fix the refill workflow so status is visible in the portal.

items.text: Failure demand: 18% call 2+ times about the same issue; find why first contact doesn't resolve it
paraphrases: 18% of callers call again about the same issue - that's failure demand to eliminate.
Improve first-contact resolution so people don't have to call back.
Repeat calls inflate volume; find why issues stay unresolved.

items.text: Handle time rose from 4.1 to 5.6 min after the EHR switch (~37% more workload); fix EHR workflow/training
paraphrases: Average handle time jumped from 4.1 to 5.6 minutes after the EHR switch - a ~37% capacity loss.
Fix EHR workflows and training to bring handle time back down.
Longer calls since March explain much of the wait; target AHT.

items.text: The 9-minute figure excludes the 21% who hang up: measure abandonment and true demand, not just answered-call wait
paraphrases: 21% abandon before answer, so the 9-minute average understates the problem.
Track abandonment rate; the wait metric only covers answered calls.
True demand includes the callers who hung up.

items.text: Menu and routing: 7 IVR options and 26% transfers waste capacity; simplify routing
paraphrases: 26% of calls get transferred - fix routing and simplify the 7-option menu.
Misrouting through the IVR adds handle time and repeat calls.
Simplify the phone tree.

items.text: Define the target properly: service level by interval (e.g., % answered within X seconds) and abandonment, not an average
paraphrases: Define success as a service level - e.g., 80% answered within 60 seconds - not an average.
Measure the wait distribution (90th percentile), not the mean.
Agree on the target metric with the COO first.

items.text: Fill the 2 vacancies first and understand attrition before adding 4 new positions
paraphrases: Backfill the 2 vacant positions before approving 4 new hires.
Understand why agents left - attrition will undo any hiring.
Fill unfilled seats first.

items.text: Callback/virtual hold improves experience and abandonment but adds no capacity; work is deferred, not removed
paraphrases: Callback reduces perceived wait and abandonment but adds no agent capacity.
Virtual hold just defers the same work into a callback queue.
The add-on doesn't fix the underlying volume.

items.text: Portal deflection only reaches the 35% with active portals; activation and other channels matter (equity, older patients)
paraphrases: Only 35% have activated the portal - deflection requires raising activation.
Portal-based fixes miss the 65% who aren't enrolled, often older patients.
Digital deflection has limited reach until portal adoption grows.
